rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a concrete and material drafting template. The child's section 3 reproduces C05's distinctive five-part sanctions machinery—loan and credit restrictions, foreign-exchange prohibitions, interbank-transfer prohibitions, property blocking, and import restrictions—in the same order and with nearly identical language. It also carries forward C05's linked donation determination, contribution prohibitions, anti-evasion provisions, specialized financial definitions, no-prior-notice finding, Treasury implementation authority, and Iran/Algiers clause, while adapting the trigger and defined term from an “ISA-sanctioned person” to a person sanctioned for specified petroleum or petrochemical support. C04 is the next strongest because it shares the Iran-specific emergency framework and some ancillary text, but it lacks the distinctive menu of five sanctions. C03 has close contemporary blocking-order language but mainly supplies standard IEEPA machinery rather than the child's central sanctions architecture.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: prohibit any United States financial institution from making loans or providing credits to the ISA-sanctioned person ...; prohibit any transactions in foreign exchange ...; prohibit any transfers of credit or payments between financial institutions ...; block all property and interests in property ...; or ... restrict or prohibit imports
shared_material.explanation: The child adopts C05's distinctive five-remedy sequence, wording, and Treasury implementation structure almost verbatim, changing the triggering criteria and sanctioned-person terminology.
